IR.rationale: A steepening term spread signals improving growth expectations or easier policy ahead, both of which support equity cash-flow expectations and risk appetite.

B.rationale: Narrowing Baa spreads together with strong high-yield returns mark easing credit conditions. Credit tends to lead equities because the two share default and discount-rate risk.

V.rationale: A high VIX embeds a large variance and equity risk premium, so elevated implied volatility has historically preceded higher subsequent equity returns.

AP.rationale: Strong emerging-market equity returns proxy for global risk appetite and world growth news that spill over into US equities with a lag.

ST.rationale: Weak momentum returns typically occur in market rebounds out of stress, when beaten-down stocks rally. This flags turning-point states for the broad market.

FX.rationale: A rising Australian dollar is a classic risk-on, carry and commodity-growth signal associated with favourable conditions for equities.

COM.rationale: Broad commodity strength reflects global demand news that is positively related to equity cash-flow expectations.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions coincide with high risk aversion and depressed prices, which raises expected returns going forward.

ENDG.rationale: Recent index performance captures short-horizon continuation or reversal in the index's own return.

IR.rationale: Falling bill yields reflect flight-to-safety demand or expected policy easing, both typical of turbulent markets.

B.rationale: Widening spreads with falling high-yield prices signal rising default risk and deleveraging. These conditions raise future equity variance through leverage and funding channels.

V.rationale: Implied volatility forecasts realised variance beyond its own history. When policy uncertainty is also high, the uncertainty is fundamental rather than transient.

AP.rationale: The leverage and volatility-feedback effect: negative market returns raise subsequent volatility more than positive returns of the same size.

ST.rationale: High reversal returns indicate costly liquidity provision and price pressure, characteristic of illiquid, volatile markets.

FX.rationale: Yen appreciation reflects safe-haven demand and carry-trade unwinding, which accompany rising risk and volatility.

COM.rationale: Oil price collapses signal demand shocks and stress among energy issuers, which tend to raise equity volatility.

MC.rationale: Financial stress indices aggregate funding, credit and volatility strains that predict persistent elevated equity variance.

ENDG.rationale: Volatility clustering means high recent realised variance carries forward.

IR.rationale: Falling bill rates reflect flight to quality and expected emergency easing, which coincide with crash-prone states.

B.rationale: Deteriorating credit marks a tightening of credit conditions that tends to precede or accompany sharp equity drawdowns.

V.rationale: High implied volatility widens the return distribution. Combined with high policy uncertainty, it marks states where large losses are more likely.

AP.rationale: Weak recent market returns raise volatility and the potential for continued forced selling, fattening the left tail.

ST.rationale: High reversal profits indicate scarce liquidity, a condition under which price declines can cascade.

FX.rationale: A rising yen together with a falling Australian dollar is the carry-unwind, risk-off configuration associated with equity tail losses.

COM.rationale: Sharp oil declines signal global demand weakness and energy-sector credit stress.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions amplify shocks through leverage and funding constraints, raising crash risk.

ENDG.rationale: Recent poor performance signals a high-volatility regime in which further extreme losses are more likely.

IR.rationale: Curve steepening on easing expectations or improving growth news tends to precede strong equity rallies.

B.rationale: High-yield bond rebounds signal returning risk appetite and often lead equity relief rallies.

V.rationale: Large gains cluster in high-volatility regimes, where both tails are wide and risk premia are elevated.

AP.rationale: Sharp rebounds typically follow selloffs, so weak recent market returns raise the chance of an extreme up move.

ST.rationale: Momentum crashes occur in violent market rebounds led by past losers, so weak momentum flags rebound states.

FX.rationale: Australian dollar strength signals a return of risk appetite and carry demand that accompanies strong equity gains.

COM.rationale: Commodity strength reflects reflationary global demand news that is associated with strong equity rallies.

MC.rationale: Elevated stress raises expected returns and the probability of policy-driven or relief rallies as stress abates.

ENDG.rationale: After weak index returns, mean reversion and higher volatility increase the chance of an extreme gain.
